rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you, that's a really generous offer, and a data analyst is exactly what we need. The project I'm scoping is a \"Frontier Incident Ledger\": a structured dataset of publicly reported safety-relevant incidents involving frontier AI models (who found them, how severe they were, whether and how fast the developer disclosed them). It's timely because of the proposed incident-reporting rule that's out for comment now. Before building anything, I want to check it isn't duplicating existing work. A concrete first task, if you're up for it (roughly 3–5 hours): - Look through the AI Incident Database and the OECD AI Incidents Monitor - Roughly how many of their entries involve frontier/general-purpose models, and what fields do they record? - Is there a gap (e.g. disclosure timing, who discovered it, severity), or would we do more good by contributing to them directly? A short bullet-point write-up by around 25 November would be perfect. I'll send you the draft schema to react to as well. Thanks again, Morgan"
rows.quote: Priya: replied to her offer from your email (privately). I asked her to do that overlap check against the existing incident databases, about 3–5 hours, with a short write-up by about 25 Nov.
